content.text:
## What I could and couldn't verify with tools

I checked my available toolset first. The only external system I have here is a **Galaxy** instance (workflow execution platform). It has **no ClinVar, HGVS, or variant-annotation lookup tool** — `search_tools_by_name("clinvar")` returned 0 hits, and the only "variant effect" hits were *gProfiler SNPense* (rs-ID → gene/coordinate mapping) and *HyphAeon-Disease* (in-silico pathogenicity prediction).

I tried to route around this via SNPense, but it needs a dataset in a Galaxy history, and I have no filesystem-write tool and no internet access to create or fetch an rs-ID input file. So **no tool call produced any number below.**

**Everything that follows is from my own knowledge, not a live database lookup.** I've flagged the items you should re-verify in ClinVar/gnomAD before putting them in a report.

## Reading the notation

| Part | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `NM_000059.4` | RefSeq transcript for BRCA2, version 4 (the MANE Select / clinical reference transcript) |
| `(BRCA2)` | Gene symbol — BRCA2, chromosome 13q13.1 |
| `c.` | Numbering in **coding** DNA (from the A of the ATG start codon) |
| `5946` | Nucleotide 5946 of the coding sequence |
| `delT` | Deletion of a single thymine |

So: **a one-base deletion of a T at coding position 5946 of BRCA2**, in exon 11 (the large central exon). Strict current HGVS writes this as `c.5946del` — the base identity is redundant. The T sits in a poly-T run, and HGVS's 3'-most-placement rule is why the position is 5946.

**Consequence:** a frameshift. Protein-level: **p.(Ser1982Argfs\*22)** — codon 1982 changes Ser→Arg, the reading frame shifts, and a premature stop codon appears 22 codons downstream. The product is truncated at ~2003 residues versus the full-length 3418, losing the DNA-binding domain and the entire C-terminal region (RAD51 interaction, nuclear localisation signal). This is a classic loss-of-function allele, the mechanism BRCA2 pathogenicity is built on.

**Legacy name: 6174delT** (old BIC nomenclature). If you search the older literature, that is the name you'll find — it is one of the most-studied variants in cancer genetics. dbSNP **rs80359550** *(recalled — verify)*.

## How serious — classification

This is **Pathogenic**, not a variant of uncertain significance. It is not a borderline call:

- Protein-truncating variant in a tumour-suppressor gene, well short of the last exon (ACMG **PVS1**), plus overwhelming case–control and segregation data (**PS4**).
- It is one of the three **Ashkenazi Jewish founder mutations** — BRCA1 c.68_69delAG (185delAG), BRCA1 c.5266dupC (5382insC), and this one. Carrier frequency ~1% in Ashkenazi Jewish individuals for this variant alone; ~1 in 40 for the three combined.
- ClinVar: Pathogenic, many independent submitters, with ENIGMA BRCA1/2 expert-panel review. *(I recall Variation ID 9325 — treat the ID as unverified.)*

## How serious — actual risk

Lifetime risks for BRCA2 pathogenic variants, from the Kuchenbaecker et al. 2017 *JAMA* prospective cohort (the standard source):

- **Female breast cancer by age 80: ~69%** (95% CI 61–77%)
- **Ovarian cancer by age 80: ~17%** (95% CI 11–25%)
- **Contralateral breast cancer, 20 years after a first breast cancer: ~26%**
- **Male breast cancer: ~7% lifetime** (vs ~0.1% baseline)
- **Prostate cancer: ~27% by age 80**, and tends toward more aggressive disease
- **Pancreatic cancer: ~2–7%** (relative risk ~3–6)

Important framing: these are *averages across carriers*. An individual's risk is modified substantially by family history and polygenic background, so a single percentage is the wrong thing to quote to a patient. Note also that BRCA2 ovarian risk is lower and later-onset than BRCA1's — which is why the recommended timing of risk-reducing surgery differs.

## Why this result is actionable, not just alarming

- **Inheritance:** autosomal dominant; 50% transmission to each child. **Cascade testing** should be offered to first-degree relatives — this is often the highest-value consequence of the result.
- **Surveillance (per NCCN):** annual breast MRI from age 25, adding mammography from 30; discussion of risk-reducing mastectomy; **risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy typically age 40–45** for BRCA2; prostate screening from age 40 in men; pancreatic surveillance if there's an affected relative.
- **Treatment:** confers homologous-recombination deficiency — predicts sensitivity to **PARP inhibitors** (olaparib, talazoparib, niraparib, rucaparib) and platinum agents. This changes therapy, not just screening.
- **Reproductive:** PGT-M is available. If both partners carry BRCA2 pathogenic variants, biallelic inheritance causes **Fanconi anaemia subtype D1 (FANCD1)**, which is severe — worth raising in reproductive counselling.

## Two things to check on the report itself

1. **Germline or somatic?** The management above applies to a *germline* finding. A somatic BRCA2 variant from a tumour panel has treatment implications but no inheritance implications, and the two are routinely confused.
2. **Transcript version.** `NM_000059.4` is the current reference; c.5946 numbering is consistent with the earlier `.3` version, so legacy reports describing 6174delT or c.5946delT refer to the same variant.

This is interpretation of nomenclature and published risk data, not medical advice — a result like this should be delivered through a genetics clinic, which is also where the family-testing conversation happens.

## ANSWER

**NM_000059.4(BRCA2):c.5946delT** = deletion of one T at position 5946 of the BRCA2 coding sequence (exon 11), causing a frameshift, **p.(Ser1982Argfs\*22)**, truncating the 3418-aa protein at ~2003 residues. Legacy name **6174delT**; an Ashkenazi Jewish founder mutation (~1% AJ carrier frequency); dbSNP rs80359550.

**Serious and clinically actionable: classified Pathogenic** (loss of function, ACMG PVS1+PS4; ClinVar Pathogenic with expert-panel review). Lifetime risks for BRCA2 carriers (Kuchenbaecker 2017 *JAMA*): breast ~69% (95% CI 61–77%), ovarian ~17% (95% CI 11–25%), male breast ~7%, prostate ~27%, pancreatic ~2–7%. Autosomal dominant, 50% to offspring → cascade testing; enhanced surveillance, risk-reducing surgery options, and **PARP-inhibitor/platinum sensitivity**.

*Source: my own knowledge — no tool lookup was possible. The only external system available was Galaxy, which has no ClinVar/HGVS annotation tool, and I had no way to create an input file for its rs-ID mapper. Verify the ClinVar Variation ID and rs number against ClinVar before citing them.*
